Describe what a multiple-stressor design can identify

Source: R/design.R
describe_design.Rd

Inspects the treatment structure of an experiment before any model is fitted: which combinations of stressor levels were observed and which are missing, which interactions each group of cells identifies, which cells are shared by several of those groups, how the experimental units are replicated and whether they were measured repeatedly. fit_responses() refuses designs with problems, and estimate_interactions() and classify_interactions() only work on the contrast sets found here.

Usage

describe_design(
  data,
  stressors,
  control,
  unit = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  max_order = NULL,
  baseline = NULL,
  background = "control",
  shared = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation. Tibbles are accepted; grouped data frames are not.

stressors

Character vector with the names of at least two stressor columns. A column may hold factors, text or numbers; every distinct value is treated as a level (a category, not a gradient).

control

Named character vector (or list) with, for every stressor, the level that represents its absence (control or ambient), e.g. c(temperature = "20", nitrate = "0"). There is no default: which level means "no stressor" is a scientific decision.

unit

Name of the column that identifies the experimental (replication) unit, or NULL (default) if every row is an independent unit. Required when time is given.

time

Name of the column with the sampling time, or NULL (default) for a single sampling.

by

Optional names of columns with other factors (population, species, experiment). Contrast sets are formed within each combination of their levels.

groups

Optional names of columns that group experimental units: blocks, whole plots of a split-plot design, rooms, incubators, header tanks or batches. For each one the checks report which stressors were applied to whole groups and whether their effects can be separated from differences among groups, and fit_responses() adds a random intercept for it when it can be estimated. Group labels must be unique within each by group (number plots 1-32, not 1-8 within each block).

max_order

Largest number of stressors in a contrast set. NULL (default) means all stressors.

baseline

Optional values of time taken before the stressors were applied (pre-treatment samplings), e.g. baseline = 0. They are kept in the models fitted by fit_responses(), where they inform the differences among units (with time_structure = "additive" they are coded as untreated, the control combination), but estimate_interactions() does not estimate or test interactions at them, so they do not enter the multiple-testing adjustment either. If the stressors were applied at different times, give a named list with the times before each one, e.g. baseline = list(drying = c(-36, -1)) when drying started on day 0 and the other stressors were applied from the start: interactions that involve drying are then not estimated at those times, and those among the other stressors are (with time_structure = "additive", drying is coded at its control there). Stressors left out of the list were applied before the first sampling. Each unit keeps the treatment it was assigned in the stressor columns. Requires time.

background

"control" (default) or "all". With "control", interactions are estimated with the stressors outside each contrast set at their control (interactions "in the absence of the other stressors"). With "all", sets are also formed with the other stressors held at each of their observed non-control levels (for example, the interaction between salinity and warming in the presence of nutrients); their reference cell is then that background combination instead of the control.

shared

Optional named character vector that marks rows shared by every group of a by column, e.g. c(regime = "both"): the rows whose regime is "both" (usually the control, sometimes also the single-stressor treatments) belong to every other level of regime. Use it when one control serves several by groups (two exposure regimes, two orders of application, upstream and downstream ponds), so that it enters the analysis once instead of being copied into each group. Contrast sets are still formed within each by group, with the shared rows supplying the cells that the group lacks; sets of different groups that use them are correlated. Each name must be a by column and each value one of its levels.

Value

An object of class must_design, a list with:

  • spec: the arguments used, with the observed levels of each stressor (control first).

  • cells: data frame with one row per observed treatment combination within each by group: context (label of the by group, "" without by), the by columns and the stressor columns (as text), cell (label), n_stressed (number of stressors not at their control), n_units, n_obs and, with time, n_times. Ordered by context, n_stressed and stressor levels.

  • missing_cells: combinations of the observed levels that are absent, within each by group (same columns as cells without the counts).

  • sets: one row per candidate contrast set, that is, per observed cell with two or more stressors away from control (and, with background = "all", per subset of two or more of those stressors): set_id, context, order (number of stressors), stressors, levels (label of the combined cell), background (levels of the stressors outside the set that are not at control, "" if none), net_identifiable, pure_identifiable (NA for two stressors, where net and pure coincide), missing_for_net, missing_for_pure, min_units (fewest units among the cells needed for the net deviation), shared (TRUE if the set uses a cell that another identifiable set also uses) and confounded (TRUE if the set involves a stressor applied to whole groups of a groups column and some of its combinations were given to a single group).

  • groups: one row per groups column: group, n_groups, between (stressors applied to whole groups), structure ("blocks", "whole_units", "confounded" or "units", see Details), groups_per_combination, units_per_group, cells_per_group and random (whether fit_responses() adds a random intercept for it).

  • set_cells: for each set, the cells it uses, with the context in which each one was observed (used by estimate_interactions()).

  • cell_use: number of identifiable sets that use each cell.

  • checks: data frame with check, severity ("problem", "warning" or "info") and message.

Details

A contrast set is the group of cells needed to estimate how a combination of stressors deviates from a null model. For a combination of the stressors in S at given levels (all other stressors at control):

  • the net deviation needs the control, each stressor of S alone and their combination. It compares the combined response with the combination of the single-stressor effects predicted by the null model.

  • the pure interaction of order |S| needs all 2^|S| combinations of S. It is what remains once all lower-order interactions are removed.

With two stressors both are the same. With three or more, the net deviation of ABC includes the pairwise interactions AB, AC and BC, so it is not a pure third-order interaction; designs that lack the pairwise cells cannot separate them.

Cells shared by several sets (typically the control in designs with several doses, or the single-stressor cells of a factorial with several levels) make the estimates of those sets correlated.

Rows shared by several by groups. When a control (or another cell) is common to several groups, copying it into each group would count its units several times. With shared, those rows form their own group (context such as "regime=both"), and each of the other groups uses its cells when it lacks them: a set of "regime=pulse" takes its control from "regime=both". The shared rows supply cells, not sets: sets are formed from the combinations observed within each group. A design with the order of application as a by column (nutrients then salinity, salinity then nutrients) and the control and single stressors shared estimates the interaction for each order.

Groups of units. A stressor that takes a single level within every group of a groups column was applied to whole groups (a whole-plot factor). Each column gets one of four structures:

  • "blocks": no stressor is applied to whole groups; treatment combinations are compared within groups (complete or incomplete blocks).

  • "whole_units": some stressors are applied to whole groups, with at least two groups per combination of their levels. For effects that involve them the replication is the number of groups, not of units, and the random intercept for the groups is needed for valid inference.

  • "confounded": some combination of the stressors applied to whole groups was given to a single group, so effects that involve them cannot be separated from differences among groups (for example, one incubator per temperature, or one nitrate level per block). The sets affected are flagged in sets$confounded; a random intercept does not remove the confounding and is not added when it cannot be estimated.

  • "units": each group holds a single unit, so the column repeats unit and is not used.

Assumptions

  • The control level of each stressor represents its absence.

  • With background = "control", interactions are estimated with the stressors outside the set at control (interactions "in the absence of the other stressors"); an interaction can differ in the presence of another stressor, which background = "all" estimates.

  • Each experimental unit receives a single treatment combination for the whole experiment. Treatments that change within a unit (sequential exposures) are reported as a problem, except stressors that start later than others, declared in baseline by stressor.

  • Units and groups not given in unit and groups are assumed independent: the design cannot reveal a shared incubator or water supply that is not recorded in the data.

  • Levels are categories. A gradient with many levels and few replicates is analysed level by level, not as a continuous predictor.

Missing values and zeros

Missing values in the stressor, unit, time, by or groups columns are an error: no treatment combination is guessed. The response is not used here.

References

Madge Pimentel, I., Albini, D., Beermann, A. J., Leese, F., Macaulay, S. J., Matthaei, C. D., Orr, J. A., Piggott, J. J., & Schäfer, R. B. (2025). Hypothesis-driven research on multiple stressors: An analytical framework for stressor interactions. Ecology and Evolution, 15, e71959. doi:10.1002/ece3.71959

Examples

# Two stressors, two levels each, four replicate jars
jars <- expand.grid(
  salinity = c("ambient", "high"),
  warming = c("no", "yes"),
  replicate = 1:4,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
jars$jar <- seq_len(nrow(jars))
design <- describe_design(
  jars,
  stressors = c("salinity", "warming"),
  control = c(salinity = "ambient", warming = "no"),
  unit = "jar"
)
design
#> <must_design> 16 rows, 2 stressors, 4 observed treatment combinations
#> Stressors (control): salinity (ambient), warming (no)
#> Unit: jar | Time: none | By: none | Groups: none
#> Contrast sets: 1 candidate(s), 1 identifiable
#> Checks:
#>   info     Experimental unit: 'jar' (16 units, each in a single treatment
#>            combination).
#>   info     Units per treatment combination: 4.
#>   info     Identifiable contrast sets (net deviation): 1 with 2 stressors.
design$sets
#>   set_id context order          stressors                      levels
#> 1    S01             2 salinity x warming salinity=high | warming=yes
#>   background net_identifiable pure_identifiable missing_for_net
#> 1                        TRUE                NA                
#>   missing_for_pure min_units shared confounded
#> 1                          4  FALSE      FALSE

# A ray design: the mixture only at matching doses
ray <- data.frame(
  a = c(0, 2, 20, 0, 0, 2, 20),
  b = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 20, 2, 20)
)
ray <- ray[rep(seq_len(nrow(ray)), each = 3), ]
ray_design <- describe_design(ray, c("a", "b"), control = c(a = "0", b = "0"))
ray_design$sets
#>   set_id context order stressors      levels background net_identifiable
#> 1    S01             2     a x b   a=2 | b=2                        TRUE
#> 2    S02             2     a x b a=20 | b=20                        TRUE
#>   pure_identifiable missing_for_net missing_for_pure min_units shared
#> 1                NA                                          3   TRUE
#> 2                NA                                          3   TRUE
#>   confounded
#> 1      FALSE
#> 2      FALSE
ray_design$missing_cells
#>   context  a  b       cell n_stressed
#> 1          2 20 a=2 | b=20          2
#> 2         20  2 a=20 | b=2          2

# Temperature applied to whole rooms, one room per temperature: its
# effects cannot be separated from differences between rooms
rooms <- expand.grid(temperature = c("15", "20"), nutrients = c("no", "yes"),
                     jar = 1:3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rooms$room <- paste0("R", rooms$temperature)
rooms$id <- seq_len(nrow(rooms))
room_design <- describe_design(rooms, c("temperature", "nutrients"),
  control = c(temperature = "15", nutrients = "no"), unit = "id",
  groups = "room")
room_design$groups
#>   group n_groups     between  structure groups_per_combination units_per_group
#> 1  room        2 temperature confounded                      1               6
#>   cells_per_group random
#> 1               2  FALSE
room_design$sets$confounded
#> [1] TRUE
